title: Taking relief for an embedded ball
question: If your ball is embedded in the ground after landing in the fairway, what are you allowed to do according to the rules?

choices.text: Play the ball as it lies, even though it is embedded.
Pick it up, clean it, and drop it within one club-length of its original spot, not nearer the hole, with no penalty.
Take a two-stroke penalty and drop it anywhere on the green.
Replace it exactly where it is embedded, without cleaning it.

explanation: If your ball is embedded in the fairway, you may lift, clean, and drop it within one club-length no nearer the hole without penalty.

juniorVersion.title: What to do if your ball is stuck in the ground
juniorVersion.question: If your ball lands in the fairway and is stuck in the ground, what can you do?

choices.text: Play the ball just as it is, even though it is stuck.
Pick up your ball, clean it, and drop it within one club-length from where it was, but not closer to the hole, with no penalty.
Add two strokes and drop your ball anywhere on the green.
Put the ball back in the same spot where it was stuck, without cleaning it.

juniorVersion.explanation: If your ball is stuck in the ground on the fairway, you can pick it up, wipe it clean, and drop it back on the ground within one club-length from where it was, but not closer to the hole. You do not get a penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: When the ball is stuck in the ground, often making a little hole.
The length of a golf club. You can use your club to measure how far you can drop the ball.
The short grass area between where you start (the tee) and the green.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show players how to check if the ball is really embedded and practise how to measure a club-length for the drop.
likelyMisconceptions: Some players might think they have to play the ball as it is, even when it is stuck.
Some might think they can just drop the ball anywhere on the green.
They may not know that the drop must be no closer to the hole.
